title: Fit a mop frame to its quick-connect handle: hold the swivelling socket square and push until the button clicks
instruction: Click the mop frame onto the handle: hold the frame's socket in line with the handle's tip and push the tip in until its spring button clicks out through the socket's window. Then let go of both and leave the mop on the bench.
context: Clicking a mop's head onto its handle is something most people who mop floors at home have done: many flat mops, spray mops and floor sweepers have a head that pushes onto the end of the handle and clicks, put on when the mop is new and again whenever a head is swapped. Here the head is a Rubbermaid HYGEN 17-inch flat mop frame and the handle its quick-connect handle; the maker's manual says to connect them "by clicking into place". The frame's socket swivels freely on a two-axis nylon joint, so one hand must hold it in line with the handle's tip while the other pushes the tip in: the button's ramp must be pushed past and the tip's lug must drop into the socket's notch before the button can spring out. With the socket left turned aside the tip misses its mouth or stops on its rim; a push that stops short leaves the button pressed inside, and the frame falls off at the first lift.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. A Rubbermaid HYGEN 17-inch Quick-Connect frame (FGQ56000YL00, 0.36 kg) lies flat on the bench on the robot's right, its middle at x 280, y -240, its long side along x: an aluminium plate 374 x 76 x 6 with black end caps (406 over the caps) and, at its middle, the nylon universal joint: a yellow swivel base on a pin along the frame 20 above the bench, carrying the black socket arm on a second pin 29 from it. The socket (34 across; bore 22.8 across and 80 deep with a 3 lead-in; a window 17 long and 7 wide in its side, 43.5 to 60.5 below the mouth; a notch 8 deep in the mouth on the window's side; mouth 124 from the arm's pin) lies folded flat toward the robot's left, window up, its axis 20 above the bench, turned 12 degrees toward the robot on the arm's pin, so its mouth is at x 254, y -90. A HYGEN Quick-Connect Short Extension Handle (FGQ74500YL00, collapsed to 640, 0.33 kg) lies along y on its ribbed locking ring and grip (both 40 across), at x 280, axis 20 above the bench: aluminium inner tube 22 across from its tip's end at y -42 to the ring at y 258, yellow outer tube 25 across, grip to its end at y 598. Near the tip, facing up: the spring button (16 long, 5 wide, 2.5 proud, ramped toward the tip; 13 to 29 from the end) and the locating lug (20 long, 10 wide, 3.5 proud; 65 to 85 from the end). Every collider is listed in README.md.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from photos and a 1.5 mm feeler gauge. Clicked: the handle's tip is in the frame's socket with its lug down in the socket's notch (the 1.5 mm gauge does not pass under the lug) and its spring button standing out through the socket's window. Still: no point of the frame or the handle moves more than 1 mm in 0.5 s. 1.0 (success): clicked, both grippers at least 3 cm clear of the frame's socket and of the handle, and still, all held for 1 s. 0.5: clicked, but not yet let go and still for 1 s. 0.25: the tip at least 30 mm inside the socket but not clicked (the button still pressed inside), let go and still for 1 s. 0: anything else, including the tip stopped on the socket's mouth or beside it, or the frame or the handle off the bench at any time.
reset_notes: Press the button in through the window and pull the frame off. Lay the frame flat at x 280, y -240, long side along x; fold its socket flat toward the robot's left, window up, and turn it 12 degrees toward the robot. Lay the handle along y on its ring and grip, tip end at y -42, button and lug up. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics. Shortcuts: no mop pad; the handle is one body, its ring and grip with 12 flats so it lies still; the button is a sprung slide; the socket is convex pieces; the demo reads poses. Estimates (no maker figure): bore 22.8 x 80 mm, 3 mm lead-in, window 17 x 7, notch 8 deep, button 16 x 5 x 2.5 (2.7 travel, 1.3 N/mm, 2 N preload), lug 20 x 10 x 3.5, arm 124, pins 20 and 29, swivel ranges, masses (0.36, 0.33 kg), frictions. README lists all.
